name: Overworld
axioms: Grow Bedrock, or create a new part, only from what real code needs now; don't design for guessed futures.
Keep an app's logic in one place, apart from the ways the app is reached.
Name every app's CLI command overworld:<app>, like overworld:dye list.
Never let an app or the shell define its own theme; all of them take the one Overworld theme.
Write the Hyprland config in Lua (hyprland.lua with the hl.* API), never in the legacy hyprlang format.
Never tie code or config to the current machine (monitors, hardware, paths, hostnames); detect it at runtime, and keep anything truly local in untracked files.
Follow SOLID principles and idiomatic modern C# conventions.
Group code into namespaces by responsibility, with folders matching the namespaces.
Prefer short names when the context makes them clear (locator, not shellLocator).
Show each new C# file, except tests, in full and one at a time, explaining only why it exists and its role, and wait for the user's review before writing the next.
Keep UI components that only one app needs inside that app; put in Overworld.Desktop only what more than one app can use.
Build the basics every desktop app has (keyboard shortcuts, text selection, copying) once in Overworld.Desktop for all apps; never add them app by app.
Write operations (their input records and Op classes) without showing them for review
Write AXAML views and view models without showing them for review
Paint the design of each new UI component in Painting (overworld:painting paint) for review before building it.
Never write comments in C# code
